design_rationale:
WORKLOG — grain_storage_desk task 0 (Cordray, identity-preserved soybean lot at Bergen Siding).

STEP 0 — draw, ledger and claim. scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/tasks/grain_storage_desk --tasks 2 printed:
  {"task": 0, "key": "farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/grain_storage_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 6]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/grain_storage_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 6, 6]}
Task 0 is therefore a two-problem tree with one prerequisite problem, and its two computations carry 6 and 5 declared factors. storage_ext_period_accrual took 6, storage_ext_invoice_settlement took 5. Nothing was occupied before this task. This task claims the money-out-of-pocket corner of the storage desk: the arrears billing of a closed period (base storage_accrual_billing) and the direct settlement of a storage invoice (base storage_charge_settlement), with the target write events storage_accrual_charged and storage_charge_settled. Left for task 1: the whole conditioning and movement corner — storage_drying_charged, storage_shrink_taken, storage_agreement_updated (receipt and pledge) and storage_loadout_recorded, under base storage_drying_and_shrink, storage_receipt_and_pledge, storage_loadout and storage_agg_capacity_across_agreements — which is four unclaimed problems, exactly the size task 1's draw calls for, on disjoint base lineage, disjoint events and disjoint tools.

Design thesis. Surface goal: 'I want to settle up the storage account on that lot today.' Scored core parameter: the money the member hands over, 2370.64. Between the two stands a policy prerequisite the customer never mentions: what she is asked to pay is fixed only after the storage account carries an accrual entry for every billing period that has closed, and the period 2026-02-04 to 2026-03-05 closed twelve days ago and was never billed. So the desk must first work out and raise that period's rent (1674.00), which is itself a six-factor computation over the deposit/shrink ledger, the grain marketing position and the time in store, and only then quote and hand over the settlement. Depth: surface goal -> prerequisite sentence in the settlement rule -> the state of the storage account (paid_through_date 2026-02-03, latest accrual period_end 2026-02-03, current date 2026-03-17) -> the accrual policy's own computation -> the settlement's computation on the world that write leaves. Breadth at each hop: the accrual reads the deposit, shrink and load-out ledger, the last arrival date, the drying history, a twelve-month deposit window, the days in store, and the member's grain settlements and open contract bushels in another difficulty; the settlement reads three classes of unpaid charge, the paid-through date, the late-charge history, the settlement history and the twelve-month deposit window.

Base-invariant card. Write 1 subject storage_accrual_charged: the only base policy whose subject intersects it is storage_accrual_billing, which declares no structured eligibility, so the inherited layer is policy_scope — the policy's whole scope of application (storage is billed in arrears for each billing period the grain stands in store on a live agreement). At frozen_time the agreement stands active (initial_state.storage_agreements.<agreement>.status = active), the free days are zero on this programme, and the period being billed closed on 2026-03-05, before frozen_time 2026-03-17; had frozen_time been 2026-03-04 the period would not yet have closed and no accrual could be raised (negative boundary), and at 2026-03-05 exactly the last day of the period has passed only at its end, so 2026-03-06 is the first day it may be billed (positive boundary). storage_accrual_billing carries no eligibility of kind time, so temporal_feasibility is empty; the period boundary above is carried by the extended rule and by the computation itself. Write 2 subject storage_charge_settled: the only base policy whose subject intersects it is storage_charge_settlement, which likewise declares no structured eligibility, so policy_scope again — the programme does not settle storage out of grain proceeds (Identity Preserved Segregated Storage: storage_settlement_from_grain_proceeds false), so the charges are invoiced and the member pays them directly, which is exactly the route this task takes. Four clauses of base are superseded, every one of them declared. storage_ext_period_accrual.overwrite names two of storage_accrual_billing's: the grouping-of-days clause (replaced by the period running from the day after the paid-through date) and the escalation clause (replaced by the three-tier time-in-store ladder that adds a mid-term step). storage_ext_invoice_settlement.overwrite names two fragments of storage_charge_settlement's late-charge sentence: 'counted in whole calendar days from the invoice date', replaced by this policy's own grace-counting sentence, and 'carries the programme's late charge once, and the late charge is added once per invoice however long the invoice then stays unpaid', replaced by its own arrears sentence. No other base clause is touched: the period minimum, the basis-fixed-by-programme rule, the free-day rule, the paid-up rule, the invoiced-and-paid-directly rule, the oldest-first rule and the settlement-clears-the-invoice-it-names rule all stand and are inherited.

Business-object card. The narrowest object is storage invoice SI-660812 standing on agreement SA-214703 (row initial_state.storage_agreements.fb7cc0c8-...), the member's only storage agreement. The correlation key written into both gold writes is (agreement_id, invoice_number). Rows that enter the settlement: the two charges already on SI-660812 (drying 488.75 on ticket T-3071904, elevation in 127.50 on the same ticket) and the accrual raised by the first write onto the same invoice. Rows excluded: every charge on SI-660412, SI-660518, SI-660644 and SI-660771, each of which carries paid_flag true and a matching settlement row (2025-11-14, 2025-12-12, 2026-01-09, 2026-02-06) — they are excluded by paid_flag, not by an author's conviction, and the compute filters on it. The deposit, shrink and load-out rows carry no money into the settlement at all; they are what the bushels on hand are backed out of.

Problem-tree card. Root problem storage_ext_invoice_settlement (the customer's surface request). One prerequisite problem, storage_ext_period_accrual, exactly as drawn. Edge storage_ext_invoice_settlement <- storage_ext_period_accrual: kind value_input; gate the compute binding unpaid_accruals; form state; prerequisite sentence, quoted verbatim from the settlement rule, 'The sum the member is asked to pay is fixed only after the storage account carries a storage accrual entry for every billing period that has closed on the agreement.' Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is 'only after', joining this policy's own result (the sum the member is asked to pay) to what it waits on; (2) the waiting side is a record-visible state — an accrual entry standing on the storage account for every closed period — and names no action, no performer and no tool; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token and no row id; (4) its strength is exactly the edge's: a hard 'only after', scoped to periods that have closed and to no others. Exactly one write in this difficulty brings that state about: storage_accrual_charged is the only event that puts an accrual entry on the storage account, and storage_ext_period_accrual is the only policy that produces it, so the reader can resolve the hop without being told a tool. Derivation the reader runs: the sentence says the sum waits on an accrual entry for every closed period; the records show the last accrual covers the period ending 2026-02-03 and the agreement is paid through 2026-02-03, while the period beginning 2026-02-04 closed on 2026-03-05, before today; therefore an accrual entry is missing; the accrual policy's own rule says the charge for a closed period is raised on the agreement's open storage invoice, so that policy's write is the one action that supplies the missing entry. Handling-time condition: every billing period whose last day has passed carries a storage accrual entry, so the accruals standing unpaid are the whole of the storage rent owed. Resolving action: the accrual write, owner agent. Seed evidence it is false at the opening: initial_state.storage_agreements.fb7cc0c8-fbe3-4813-a3fb-03fdb4aca0a1.paid_through_date = 2026-02-03 and initial_state.storage_charges.ff6bca45-60f3-488c-b5c3-ac464ba4d3d5.period_end = 2026-02-03, the latest accrual on the account, against frozen_time 2026-03-17. Topological order: storage_ext_period_accrual then storage_ext_invoice_settlement. No parallel edges, so order_uniqueness is trivial and recorded as such. Deletion sensitivity, actually run: skipping the accrual write leaves unpaid_accruals at 0.00, unpaid_classes at 2, cleared_charges at 616.25 and the settlement's scored amount at 616.25 + 15.00 - 3.08 + 76.84 = 705.01 instead of 2370.64. The customer's own write is the root: settle_storage_charges_68342e7f is owner=user, unlocked by the desk and run by the member herself.

Factor card — storage_ext_period_accrual (6 factors; handling-time world = the opening world, since this problem has no prerequisite).
  billed_bushels_basis (method) — tier taken: the programme keeps the lot out of the house bin (commingling_allowed false) and the bushels on hand, 38155.01, stand below the 60000 bushels of space the agreement reserves, so the period is billed on the reserved space. Evidence rows: the four deposits (37dc7251 12480.00, da72adee 11930.00, 69674d0c 9760.00, 9d464bb9 4250.00) and the three shrink lines (b22f2e28 144.77, 9e1084a8 81.12, 430ffe68 39.10). Baseline: the bushels free to move, 38155.01, which gives 1064.52.
  days_counted_convention (method) — tier taken: the last load into store arrived on 2026-02-14, eleven days after the paid-through date and so inside the period, and no bushels left store inside it, so the days run from 2026-02-14 through 2026-03-05, twenty days. Evidence: deposit 9d464bb9 charge_date 2026-02-14, no storage_loadout_recorded row on the account. Baseline: the whole 30-day period, which gives 2511.00.
  marketing_carry_credit (method, multi-source, cross-difficulty grain) — tier taken: 27800.00 bushels settled on the member's grain contracts in the last twelve months (grain_ledger 296e3b02 12400.00 on 2025-11-21, 141a1089 9800.00 on 2026-01-16, 1ce827b7 5600.00 on 2026-02-27) is at or above twenty thousand, and grain contract GC-118406 (2d3a0d33, status active, commodity soybeans) still carries 8000 open bushels, so the twenty days are halved to ten. Baseline: every day counted, twenty days, which gives 3348.00.
  condition_rate_step (parameter) — tier taken: the grade of record is us_no_2, not sample grade, but the storage account carries three drying passes inside the last six months (cc2b971e 2025-10-06, d9585489 2025-10-12, 95ad1a2a 2026-02-14), so the second tier holds by its 'or' limb and the watch step of 0.00020 is added. Baseline: no step, which gives 1554.00.
  volume_rate_reduction (parameter) — tier taken: 38420.00 bushels were taken into store under the agreement in the last twelve months, at or above eighteen thousand, so the large reduction of 0.00015 comes off. Baseline: no reduction, which gives 1764.00.
  time_in_store_rate_step (parameter) — tier taken: 162 days in store from 2025-10-06 to 2026-03-17 is past the mid-term day count of 120 but not past the programme's escalation point of 365, so the posted rate is stepped up by 12 percent to 0.002744. Baseline: the posted rate 0.00245 as it stands, which gives 1500.00.
  Near-miss planted for the reading of the ladders: deposit 69674d0c (T-3062017, 9760.00 bushels, 2025-10-19) went into store without being run through the dryer, so it carries no drying pass and no shrink line, so an agent who assumes every load was dried overstates the shrink and understates the bushels; and the same load is the one that tempts a reader of days_counted_convention, since it is the last October arrival while the arrival that actually falls inside the period is the February one. The agreement header carries a stale cache: bushels_in_store is 38420.00, the gross of the deposits with the three shrink lines never rolled in, while the ledger backs out 38155.01; no rule reads the header field, and the rule says so in terms.
  Whole-baseline fall-back (every factor at its fall-through): 2804.39, against gold 1674.00.

Factor card — storage_ext_invoice_settlement (5 factors; handling-time world = the opening world plus the accrual write).
  charge_scope_drawn_in (method) — tier taken: the programme does not settle storage out of grain proceeds and three classes of charge stand unpaid (accrual 1674.00, elevation in 127.50, drying 488.75), so every unpaid charge is drawn in, 2290.25. Baseline: accruals and handling only, 1801.50, giving 1884.33.
  grace_counting_convention (method) — tier taken: statements reach this member through the portal and by email, so the grace period is counted from the paid-through date 2026-02-03; 42 days less the 10-day grace leaves 32 days past grace. Baseline: counted from the most recent charge raised on the account, which after the accrual write is today, giving 0 days past grace and a settlement of 2332.74.
  arrears_charge_added (parameter, multi-source) — tier taken: a charge stands past its grace period and no late charge has been raised on the account within the last twelve months (no row carries charge_type late_payment), so the programme's 60.00 late charge is set aside and only the 15.00 arrears notice fee is added. Baseline: nothing added, 2355.64.
  prompt_settlement_allowance (parameter, multi-source) — tier taken: a charge does stand past grace, so the full rate fails, but four storage settlements stand on the account inside six months of frozen_time (608895d2 on 2025-11-14, c3147f27 on 2025-12-12, e3c9a151 on 2026-01-09 and 7d6f20a1 on 2026-02-06), so the 'or' limb holds and the modest rate of 0.005 is allowed: 11.45 off. Baseline: no allowance, 2382.09.
  per_unit_retain_collected (parameter) — tier taken: the programme earns patronage and 38420.00 bushels were taken into store in the last twelve months, at or above fifteen thousand, so the retain is 0.0020 per bushel on all of them, 76.84. Baseline: no retain, 2293.80.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 1801.50, against gold 2370.64.

Seed card — why each class of row exists and what its removal changes. The customer row is the only one; it carries the two credentials verification uses. The agreement row fixes the programme (Identity Preserved Segregated Storage: rate 0.00245, period 30 days, minimum 75.00, escalation after 365 days, capacity share 60000, commingling false, patronage eligible, retain 0.0020, grace 10, late fee 60.00, statements by portal and email, settles from grain proceeds false), the paid-through date that both the prerequisite and the grace count read, the grade of record, and the deliberately stale bushels_in_store cache. The four deposits and three shrink lines are what on_hand and the twelve-month volume window are backed out of: drop the February deposit and the days convention falls back to the whole period and the volume tier stays; drop a shrink line and on_hand and the baseline figure move. The three drying rows carry the condition step (drop the February pass and the six-month count falls to two, still above zero, so the tier holds — it is the grade limb that is absent, which is the point of the 'or') and 488.75 of unpaid money into the settlement. The four accruals are the history that makes the missing fifth visible: each is paid, each carries its own invoice, and the last one ends on the paid-through date. Each was worked out as the policy in force would have worked it at its own charge date - billed on the 60000 bushels of reserved space, at 0.00250 a bushel a day for the first three periods and 0.00279 for the fourth once 120 days in store had run, over the days the movement convention counted (18 for the first period, whose last load arrived inside it, and 30 for the others), carried at three quarters of them by the marketing credit and at half of them for the fourth once 22200 bushels had been settled - so the account's own history teaches the algorithm this task scores rather than a plainer one. The elevation-in row carries 127.50 of unpaid handling and, with the drying row, makes unpaid_classes three. The four settlement rows are what the prompt allowance's second limb reads; delete the 2026-02-06 one and the allowance falls to nothing. The grain contract and the three grain settlement rows are the cross-difficulty evidence: delete them and the carry credit falls to its fall-through and the accrual becomes 3348.00. Automatic-clause check: base's daily accrual is exactly what this task discharges; the escalation point (365 days) is not reached; max_storage_days is 400 and the lot has stood 162, so no obligation to move the grain is lit; late_payment_grace_days has run, and the arrears charge that follows is carried inside this task's settlement rather than left dangling; no receipt is outstanding (reserved_bushels 0.00, warehouse_receipt_number empty), so no pledge obligation is lit; insurance_on_file is true, as the programme's entry gate requires.

Persona design. Delia Cordray speaks first about the invoice standing open and about wanting it cleared before planting money goes out; she states the target object (the identity-preserved bean lot at Bergen Siding), the timing (today), and the authorisation boundary in her own words — the desk may read and work out, but she will put the payment through herself from the member portal. She volunteers no figure and cannot produce one; asked, she says the portal only shows the invoice open. Identity comes out only on request, in the order a real caller gives it: name and farm first, the membership number off the statement, then the mobile number and the last four of the tax number. Her one natural trap is a mild 'that sounds bigger than the ones I have been paying' if the total surprises her, which asks for a re-check against the account and never supplies a number, a formula or a step. Nothing in her script names the accrual, the closed period, the unbilled rent, or any notion that something must be done first. Her arc closes exactly where the evaluation closes: she runs the payment when it is handed to her, reports what came back, hears that the invoice is settled, and ends the call without naming a further errand.

Reachability, turn by turn. She gives farm and membership number when asked (step 0 locates on both), then two credentials (step 1 clears identity at K=2). The desk lists her storage agreements (step 2) and reads the storage account (step 3) — which is where the four paid accruals, the paid-through date, the open invoice SI-660812 and its two unpaid charges all become visible, and where the missing fifth period becomes visible as a fact rather than a hint. The grain contract and grain ledger reads (steps 4 and 5) supply the carry-credit tier. The accrual is unlocked and raised (steps 6 and 7); the settlement tool is unlocked and handed over, and the member runs it (steps 8 and 9). Everything is synchronous under one frozen_time: no diagnosis, no delivery, no clearing, no manual review, no future date. Every value the two writes consume is either computed by policy on the handling-time world or copied from a return already in the transcript: the agreement id from step 2, the invoice number SI-660812 from step 3, the two dates from the paid-through date plus the programme's period length.

Verification. The handling-time recomputation was run with the gate's own evaluator (build_env / eval_compute from skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py) over this initial_state, then over the world after the real accrual tool had been replayed. Output: storage_ext_period_accrual result 1674.00 with bindings deposited 38420.0, shrunk 264.99, on_hand 38155.01, billed_bushels 60000, period_days 30, last_arrival_offset 11, period_days_counted 20, settled_bushels_12m 27800.0, open_contract_bushels 8000.0, chargeable_days 10, drying_passes_6m 3, condition_step_rate 0.0002, volume_deposits_12m 38420.0, volume_rate_step 0.00015, days_in_store 162, posted_rate 0.002744, daily_rate 0.00279, gross_charge 1674.0; per-factor baselines 1064.52 / 2511.00 / 3348.00 / 1554.00 / 1764.00 / 1500.00 and whole baseline 2804.39. Then storage_ext_invoice_settlement result 2370.64 with unpaid_accruals 1674.0, unpaid_handling 127.5, unpaid_drying 488.75, unpaid_classes 3, cleared_charges 2290.25, days_unpaid 42, days_past_grace 32, late_charges_12m 0, late_charge 15.0, settlements_6m 4, prompt_allowance_rate 0.005, prompt_allowance 11.45, crop_year_deposits 38420.0, retain_charge 76.84; per-factor baselines 1884.33 / 2332.74 / 2355.64 / 2382.09 / 2293.80 and whole baseline 1801.50. Both equal the declared expected values and the gold arguments.

Two-way equivalence. Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice quotes its rule sentence in compute_basis — the three ledger sums and on_hand quote the backing-out sentence, billed_bushels quotes the space ladder, the arrival and exit offsets quote the movement ladder, the grain reads quote the carry-credit ladder, the drying count quotes the condition ladder, the twelve-month deposit sum quotes the volume ladder, days_in_store quotes the counting sentence, posted_rate quotes the time-in-store ladder, daily_rate quotes the stacking sentence, and gross_charge and result quote the charge sentence. Reverse sweep of the accrual rule: 'billed in arrears, one period at a time' -> period_days and the period sentence; 'raised on the agreement's open storage invoice' -> the invoice_number argument, traced on the call; 'rounded to the nearest cent' -> RND on gross_charge and result; 'where the product falls under the programme's period minimum' -> MX against P('storage_minimum_charge_usd'); 'carried to five decimal places' -> RND(..., 5) on daily_rate; 'the step being added and the reduction subtracted on the same posted rate rather than one acting on the other's result' -> the single additive expression in daily_rate; every ladder sentence -> its ternary chain. Same sweep on the settlement rule: the standard-method sentence, 'the settlement is drawn for the storage accruals and the handling charges standing unpaid on the invoice named, and that total, rounded to the nearest cent, is what the member pays to clear the account' -> the two unpaid sums and the rounding on them; 'Where the account has earned an arrears charge it is added to that total ... in that order, the sum of the four rounded to the nearest cent' -> the result expression; 'worked out on the charges drawn into the settlement and on nothing else, and is rounded to the nearest cent before it is taken off' -> prompt_allowance; 'cleared oldest first' -> the whole-invoice scope, which leaves no older charge open; each ladder -> its chain. No sentence of either rule is left unclaimed and no filter in either compute is absent from the prose.

Draft recomputation from the visible context alone, with the extended yaml, compute, expected and gold masked: from the policy prose that will be published, the member is asking to clear an open storage invoice; the account shows storage billed and paid through 2026-02-03 and the newest accrual ending on that date, so the period 2026-02-04 to 2026-03-05, which closed before today, has no entry; the rent for it must be worked out first. Reading the published ladders against the records gives reserved space 60000 bushels, twenty days counted from the 14 February load, halved to ten by the carry credit, and a rate of 0.00245 stepped 12 percent to 0.002744, plus 0.00020 for condition, less 0.00015 for volume, carried to five places as 0.00279; 0.00279 x 60000 x 10 = 1674.00, above the 75.00 minimum. Then the settlement: all three classes of unpaid charge, 2290.25; 42 days from the paid-through date less 10 days grace is 32 past grace; no late charge in twelve months, so 15.00; a settlement inside six months, so 0.005 of 2290.25, 11.45 off; patronage retain 0.0020 on 38420.00 bushels, 76.84; 2290.25 + 15.00 - 11.45 + 76.84 = 2370.64. That agrees with gold, and no second reading of the published text reaches a different figure: the space ladder, the movement ladder and the carry-credit ladder each select exactly one tier on these records, and the two dates of the period are fixed by the paid-through date and the programme's period length.

Gates run after this task was written: check_extended --task 0, check_task_tools --task 0, replay_tasks --task 0, check_solvability --task 0, check_compute --task 0, check_grounding --task 0, check_cache_diff --task 0 and check_cross_fire --task 0; outputs recorded in the session log. check_traceability is deferred until the knowledge base is rendered, since it reads the published documents.

REVISION 2 - answering the round-1 policy-task audit (audits/policy_task/grain_storage_desk/0.md and _difficulty.md).

F1 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, undeclared override of base's late-charge provision). Symptom: storage_ext_invoice_settlement declared overwrite: [] while its own rule counts the grace period from somewhere other than the invoice date and says the programme's late charge is set aside, so base's sentence and the extended rule both stood and gave two defensible settlements on this world, 2415.64 against the scored 2370.64. Root cause: the departure was real and the policy named no base clause for it. Change: two overwrite entries against storage_charge_settlement, quoting the anchor fragment and the amount fragment of that base sentence and naming the two sentences of this policy's own rule that take their place. Nothing in the computation moved - the scored settlement is still 2370.64 - but it is now the only figure the charter in force entails, the base clause that produced 2415.64 being declared retired. Re-run: check_extended --task 0 OK (the overwrite quotations are verbatim on both sides), check_compute --task 0 recomputes 2370.64.

F2 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, the settlement's baseline). Symptom: baseline.rule named an arrears charge, an allowance and a retain without stating a default for any of them, and baseline.params named late_payment_grace_days, late_payment_fee_usd and per_unit_retain_per_bushel_usd, none of which the declared baseline uses; a reader of the computation document alone reached 1937.84 while the declared baseline bindings give 1801.50. Root cause: the baseline paragraph summarised the whole rule instead of stating the standard method. Change: the rule's composite sentence was split into a standard-method sentence and a variation sentence, and the baseline now carries the standard method alone - the storage accruals and the handling charges standing unpaid on the invoice named, that total rounded to the nearest cent - with baseline.params: [], since that method uses no programme parameter. The computation document now yields 1801.50, exactly computations[1].baseline_result, and nothing else. Re-run: check_compute --task 0 OK, baseline_result 1801.50 and all five factor sensitivities unchanged.

Task-local item (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, a false world assertion). Symptom: computations[1].factor_trace[3] said COUNT of settlement rows inside six months is one, naming only the 2026-02-06 row; the world holds four. Root cause: the line named the row that makes the tier hold rather than the count the binding returns. Change: it now names all four rows with their dates. The tier taken and the scored value are unaffected, since the second tier holds by its second limb on any count above zero.

O12 (the seeded charge history was not produced by the policy the tasks score). Judged a genuine defect rather than an observation: a solver reconciling the account would have found four accruals equal to the plain posted rate times the bushels on hand times thirty days, which teaches the baseline and contradicts the ladders that same solver is asked to apply. Change: the four seeded accruals were recomputed as the policy in force would have worked them at their own charge dates - 2100.00, 3450.00, 3450.00 and 2511.00, each on the 60000 bushels of reserved space, at 0.00250 for the first three and 0.00279 for the fourth, over 14, 23, 23 and 15 days after the movement convention and the marketing credit - and the four settlement rows now equal the invoices they clear (4923.65, 3450.00, 3450.00, 2511.00). No scored value moves: the settlement's unpaid sums read only rows with paid_flag false and its settlement count reads only dates, so the accrual is still 1674.00 and the settlement still 2370.64 at their own handling times.

O11 (the bushels_in_store header contradicts its declared schema meaning). Judged and kept. The header is a deliberately stale cache, declared here and in seed_consistency; the instantiate skill allows exactly this one exception to the seed's schema invariants, every policy of this difficulty says in terms that the bushels are backed out of the storage account and never read off the agreement header, and the near-miss it creates is one of the two this task rests on. Removing it would delete a trap the task is built on without making any rule truer.

O7 (the baseline sentence and the ladder sentence are both unconditional in surface form). Partly answered by the F2 change: the settlement's standard-method sentence now states what is drawn in and what the member pays, and every sentence that varies it opens with a conditional. The remainder is the framework's baseline/factor split and belongs to the render step.

O13 (verify_member_identity's docstring and body disagree). Outside this write domain and the blueprint is frozen. Recorded, no action: this persona clears the threshold on two credentials that are not the membership number (the mobile number and the tax-id last four), so nothing here turns on it.

Persona (observation 3 in 0.md). The line "Once the desk tells you the account has been brought up to date and gives you the total to pay" told a reader of the persona that the account would be brought up to date, which is the shape of the prerequisite. It now reads "Once the desk gives you the total to pay", which keeps the passive reaction and its trigger and says nothing about what the desk did first.

Observations 4 and 5 of 0.md (the near-miss shrink row doing double duty, and the world/schema and history/policy notes) are answered above under O11 and O12; the double duty of storage_charges[430ffe68-...] is deliberate and unchanged - it is the near-miss for the day-count convention and one of the three rows that separate the backed-out bushels from the header.

REVISION 4 - answering the round-3 policy-task audit (audits/policy_task/grain_storage_desk/0.md and _difficulty.md, revision_3).

F6 does not reach this task: the divergent ladder belongs to storage_ext_drying_pass, which task 1 claims. user_scenario:
You are Delia Cordray, fifty-one, who farms about two thousand two hundred acres of corn and food-grade soybeans with her brother out of Bergen, and who has been a Prairie Ridge member since her father put her on the books. You are calling the member services desk from the shop office with the laptop open in front of you, a little hurried because the seed truck is due, but friendly about it: you and the co-op go back a long way and you talk to the desk the way you talk to a neighbour.

What you want is simple, and you say it in your own words near the start: the identity-preserved bean lot you have sitting at Bergen Siding has a storage invoice standing open on it, and before planting money starts going out the door you want to settle up the storage account on that lot today and be done with it. You are happy for the desk to pull up whatever records it needs and to work out what the figure comes to, but the payment itself is yours to make: you say plainly that you will put it through yourself from the member portal once the desk has told you what to pay and set it up for you, and you will not have the desk paying it on your behalf. You are not asking for anything else to be done to the lot; the beans stay where they are.

You genuinely do not know what the account comes to. If you are asked, you say the portal only ever shows you that the invoice is still open, that you paid the last one back in early February, and that you have never sat down and added the conditioning charges up. You have no idea how the elevator works the rent out and you do not pretend to. If the number the desk gives you sounds larger than the ones you have been paying, you say so once, mildly, in the way of someone checking rather than arguing, and ask whether it has been worked out against the account; if the desk stands by it and explains it, you accept it and move on. You never offer a figure of your own.

You do not volunteer your details. When the desk asks who is calling you give your name and say you farm as Cordray Brothers Farms; if it wants the membership number you read it off the statement as M-22418. Only when you are asked for something more to prove it is you do you give the mobile number the co-op has for you, 5150224417, and, if a second thing is wanted, the last four of the tax number on the W-9, which are 2247. If the desk asks when the membership was accepted you say 2009-04-14, and if it asks for the email you give dcordray@cordraybrothersfarms.com, but you do not reel any of that off unprompted. If you are asked which lot you mean, you say it is the food-grade beans from last fall at Bergen Siding, and that it is the only grain you have in store anywhere. If you are asked whether you want any of this taken out of grain proceeds, you say you have always just paid the storage bills yourself and would rather do that now. If you are asked for anything you have no way of knowing, such as which charges sit on which invoice or what grade the bin is carried at, you say the desk will have to read that off its own records because you could not tell it from the portal.

Once the desk gives you the total to pay, you say that is fine and to set it up. When the desk hands the payment over to you, you run it yourself for the amount you were given, exactly as the desk states it, and then you tell the desk what came back. When you hear that the payment is recorded and the invoice is settled, you are satisfied: you thank whoever you have been speaking to, say that is one thing off the list before planting, and end the call there. You do not ask for anything to be sent to you and you do not raise a second piece of business.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull up the membership profile from the two things the caller states about herself, the number off her statement and the name the farm trades under, so the rest of the call works on one member record.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the member's internal reference nothing else on the account can be looked up, and identity cannot be checked against a profile that has not been found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Establish that the caller is the member whose storage account is about to be read and charged, by checking the mobile number and the last four of the tax number against the profile.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must clear before any account business is transacted, and both writes of this call move money on the member's account.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the member's storage agreements and read the one holding the food-grade beans: its programme, status, facility, the date storage is billed and paid through, the grade of record, the bushels pledged and the bushels the header claims.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The programme fixes the rate, period length, reserved space, minimum, grace, late charge, retain and settlement route; the paid-through date fixes both the period to be billed and the days past grace; reserved_bushels feeds the free-bushel reading of the billed-bushels rule.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole storage account: every deposit and its ticket, every drying pass and shrink line, the four accruals already raised with their periods and invoices, the elevation-in charge, and the settlements that cleared the earlier invoices.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The bushels on hand are backed out of these rows, the last arrival date decides the days counted, the drying passes decide the condition step, the twelve-month deposits decide the volume reduction and the retain, the unpaid rows decide what the settlement draws in, and the newest accrual's period end is what shows that a closed period carries no entry.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's grain marketing contracts to see whether an active contract for the same commodity still carries open bushels.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The open bushels on an active soybean contract are one of the two conditions of the carry credit that decides how many of the days counted are billed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's grain ledger and total the bushels settled on her marketing contracts over the last twelve months.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The settled bushels are the other condition of the carry credit; without them the days billed cannot be decided between halved, three quarters and full.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk's own tool for raising a closed period's storage rent so it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Raise the storage rent for the billing period 2026-02-04 to 2026-03-05 on the agreement's open storage invoice, so the storage account carries an accrual entry for every period that has closed.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: storage_ext_period_accrual is the only policy that computes the storage rent of a closed period, and its result 1674.00 is the amount this call carries; until it lands the accruals standing unpaid are not the whole of the rent owed.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.agreement_id: The internal reference of storage agreement SA-214703, read from the return of the storage agreement lookup at action 2, which is the member's only storage agreement and the only one holding food-grade beans at Bergen Siding; the basis is the agreement lookup's own description, 'Retrieve a member's grain storage agreements', and no other agreement row exists for this member, so any correct agent converges on it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_number: SI-660812. The basis is the accrual rule's sentence 'the charge for a closed period is raised on the agreement's open storage invoice, the invoice carrying the charges the member has not yet settled', and the storage account read at action 3 shows exactly one invoice carrying unpaid charges: the drying pass of 488.75 and the elevation in of 127.50 both carry invoice SI-660812 with paid_flag false, while SI-660412, SI-660518, SI-660644 and SI-660771 each carry paid_flag true and a matching settlement row. The tool's own contract requires the number 'taken exactly as it appears on the storage account rows it is to join', so the value is copied character for character from that return and no other candidate remains.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.period_start: 2026-02-04, computed by policy: the extended rule states that 'A billing period runs the programme's period length in calendar days beginning the day after the date storage was last billed and paid through', and the agreement read at action 2 gives paid_through_date 2026-02-03, so the period opens the next day.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.period_end: 2026-03-05, computed by policy from the same sentence: the period runs the programme's period length, 30 calendar days for this programme, from 2026-02-04, so its last day counted inclusively is 2026-03-05, which has already passed at frozen_time 2026-03-17 and is therefore billable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.bushels: 60000.00, the quantity the period is billed on. The billed-bushels rule selects between three bases: this programme keeps the lot out of the house bin (commingling is not allowed on it) and the bushels on hand backed out of the storage account are 38420.00 taken in less 264.99 of shrink less nothing loaded out, 38155.01, which stands below the 60000 bushels of space the agreement reserves, so the first tier holds and the period is billed on the reserved space. The header figure of 38420.00 is not what any rule reads.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 1674.00, the result of storage_ext_period_accrual on the opening world. The daily rate starts at the programme's posted 0.00245; 162 days have run from the storage start date 2025-10-06 to 2026-03-17, past the mid-term count of 120 but not past the programme's escalation point of 365, so the rate is stepped up 12 percent to 0.002744; the condition step adds 0.00020 because three drying passes stand on the account inside the last six months; the volume reduction takes off 0.00015 because 38420.00 bushels were taken into store in the last twelve months; added and subtracted on the same posted rate and carried to five decimal places that is 0.00279. The days: the last load arrived 2026-02-14, eleven days after the paid-through date and so inside the period, and no bushels left store inside it, so the days run from that arrival through 2026-03-05, twenty days; 27800.00 bushels settled on the member's grain contracts in the last twelve months and 8000 open bushels on an active soybean contract put her on the top tier of the carry credit, so the twenty days are halved to ten. 0.00279 x 60000.00 x 10 = 1674.00, above the programme's 75.00 period minimum, so the product stands.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the member's own payment action and hand it over to her, since she stated that the payment is hers to make.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair for a customer-owned write; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The member pays off storage invoice SI-660812 herself for the sum the desk has quoted, and the payment is recorded against that invoice on her storage account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: storage_ext_invoice_settlement is the only policy that computes what a member clearing the storage account pays, and it is evaluated on the world the accrual write leaves; the member performs it in person because disposing of her own money is her act.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.agreement_id: The same storage agreement reference read from the agreement lookup at action 2 and already used by the accrual at action 7; the invoice being cleared stands on that agreement and on no other, so there is one candidate.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_number: SI-660812, copied character for character from the storage account rows read at action 3 and from the accrual receipt returned at action 7, which names the invoice the rent was billed on. Base storage_charge_settlement fixes that 'Settlement clears the invoice it names and nothing else', and SI-660812 is the only invoice on the account carrying charges with paid_flag false, so no other invoice can be the one being cleared.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 2370.64, the result of storage_ext_invoice_settlement on the world as it stands after the accrual of action 7. The charges drawn in: the programme does not settle storage out of grain proceeds and three classes stand unpaid, so all of them come in - the 1674.00 accrual just raised, 127.50 of elevation in and 488.75 of drying, 2290.25 in all. The arrears charge: statements reach this member through the portal and by email, so the grace is counted from the paid-through date 2026-02-03, 42 days to frozen_time less the programme's 10-day grace leaves 32 days past grace; no late charge has been raised on the account in twelve months, so the programme's 60.00 late charge is set aside and the 15.00 arrears notice fee is added. The allowance: a charge does stand past grace, but a storage settlement cleared on 2026-02-06, inside six months, so the second limb holds and the modest rate of 0.005 on 2290.25 is 11.45 off. The retain: the programme earns patronage and 38420.00 bushels were taken in over twelve months, above fifteen thousand, so 0.0020 a bushel is 76.84. 2290.25 + 15.00 - 11.45 + 76.84 = 2370.64.

edges.condition: Every billing period whose last day has passed on the agreement carries a storage accrual entry on the storage account, so that the accruals standing unpaid are the whole of the storage rent owed.
edges.policy_source: The sum the member is asked to pay is fixed only after the storage account carries a storage accrual entry for every billing period that has closed on the agreement.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time 2026-03-17 the agreement is billed and paid through 2026-02-03 and the newest accrual on the storage account covers the period ending 2026-02-03. The next billing period, 2026-02-04 to 2026-03-05, closed twelve days before frozen_time and carries no accrual entry at all, so the accruals standing unpaid on the account, 0.00, are not the whole of the storage rent owed.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The accrual write raises a storage_accrual_charged row for 2026-02-04 to 2026-03-05 with amount 1674.00 and paid_flag false, so every closed period then carries an entry and the settlement's unpaid_accruals binding moves from 0.00 to 1674.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single edge and therefore a single topological order: the accrual is raised, then the settlement is quoted and paid. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder, so no second terminal state is reachable; and the order cannot be swapped, because a settlement drawn before the accrual lands would clear 616.25 instead of 2290.25 and would leave the period's rent standing open afterwards.
prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names storage_ext_period_accrual, the closed billing period, the unbilled rent, the paid-through date or any notion that something must be settled first. Delia states only that an invoice stands open on the lot and that she wants to clear it, says she has no idea what it comes to and has never added the charges up, and reacts to the prerequisite only after the desk raises it: she agrees to the total she is given, and if it sounds larger than the ones she has been paying she asks once whether it was worked out against the account, supplying no number, no mechanism and no step.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the accrual write and replaying everything else leaves unpaid_accruals at 0.00 instead of 1674.00, unpaid_classes at 2 instead of 3, cleared_charges at 616.25 instead of 2290.25, the prompt allowance at 3.08 instead of 11.45, and the settlement's scored amount at 705.01 instead of 2370.64; the terminal state also lacks the accrual row itself.

prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Neither tool validates the prerequisite. settle_storage_charges_68342e7f in task_tools.py reads the agreement only to copy the owning member onto the row and then calls ctx.create unconditionally: it does not look at the accruals standing on the account, does not compare the paid-through date with the clock, raises no error and returns the same confirmation line whether or not the closed period has been billed. charge_storage_accrual_0a686c89 is equally unconditional. An agent that skips the accrual gets a clean receipt for 705.01 and a different terminal hash, which is the only consequence.

The baseline is the bushels free to move, 38155.01, which would have given 1064.52.

days_counted_convention (method): the last deposit 9d464bb9 is dated 2026-02-14, eleven days after the paid-through date 2026-02-03 and so inside the 30-day period, and COUNT of load-out rows is zero, so the first tier holds and the days run from that arrival through the period's last day, 20 days. The baseline is the whole period, 30 days, which would have given 2511.00.

marketing_carry_credit (method, cross-difficulty grain): grain_ledger rows 296e3b02 12400.00, 141a1089 9800.00 and 1ce827b7 5600.00 settle 27800.00 bushels inside twelve months, at or above the twenty thousand of the top tier, and grain contract 2d3a0d33 (GC-118406) is active on soybeans with 8000 open bushels, so both limbs of the conjunction hold and the 20 days are halved to 10. The baseline is every day counted, 20, which would have given 3348.00.

The baseline is no step, which would have given 1554.00.

volume_rate_reduction (parameter): the same four deposits total 38420.00 bushels inside twelve months, at or above eighteen thousand, so the large reduction 0.00015 comes off the posted rate. The baseline is no reduction, which would have given 1764.00.
